purpose: Machine-readable verification ledger for the M3 graded-probe reader design. Verified by web_search against publisher/index records on 2026-11-27; full-text claims are not asserted where only abstracts/index records were available.

sources.title: Encoding specificity and retrieval processes in episodic memory
sources.mapping: Use the source-native label that was encoded at write time as the retrieval cue; a redundant post-hoc stamp is not the encoded trace.
sources.verification: APA PsycNet record + PhilPapers + Loterre thesaurus quotation of p.369; DOI consistent across records.

sources.title: Levels of processing versus transfer appropriate processing
sources.journal: Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior
sources.mapping: The forced-choice surface must overlap the encoding operations; read the encoded label rather than a parallel stamp.
sources.verification: APA PsycNet record + Semantic Scholar + OpenAlex; DOI consistent.

sources.title: Contextual prerequisites for understanding: Some investigations of comprehension and recall
sources.journal: Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior
sources.mapping: A schema supplied before encoding changes what can later be recalled: schema acts as a retrieval cue, not only an encoding aid.
sources.verification: APA PsycNet record + full paper PDF (Yale memory lab) + Springer review quoting the finding.

sources.title: Recall of previously unrecallable information following a shift in perspective
sources.journal: Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior
sources.mapping: A schema activated at recall alone changes what is retrieved; M2 subject-side evidence is a legitimate read cue independent of encoding.
sources.verification: ERIC record ED142974 + paper PDF (Illinois). No DOI was confirmed in this session; cited without one rather than guessed.

sources.title: Schemas and memory consolidation
sources.mapping: One-trial assimilation requires a pre-existing schema: M2 is a separate necessary condition, not a restatement of M1.
sources.verification: Science publisher page + CiNii + PubMed commentary (PMC2271071).

sources.title: Negation and its impact on the accessibility of text information
sources.mapping: Explicit negation reduces accessibility of the negated concept; an admitted negated (subject,label) fact vetoes that label.

sources.title: 'A good Arab is not a dead Arab': On the accessibility of negated concepts
sources.journal: In Kecskes & Horn (Eds.), Explorations in Pragmatics
sources.mapping: Negated concepts are not unconditionally suppressed; therefore the veto is scoped to an explicitly negated, provenance-admitted (subject,label), never a global word ban.
sources.verification: DOI listed in Cambridge Core reference list and in Giora's own PDF; index-level, not full text.

sources.title: Source monitoring
sources.mapping: Trust is evaluated from provenance, never from confidence/familiarity; untrusted records cannot admit or veto.

sources.title: A theory of lexical access in speech production
sources.mapping: Commit to the proposition before form encoding: structural deferral returns an already-admitted production pick untouched.
sources.verification: Cambridge Core publisher record + APA PsycNet. NOTE: earlier RAVANA docs quoted pages 1-63; corrected here to 1-38.
